# TinyRustLM Full Agent Text

> Condensed full machine-readable bundle for TinyRustLM plain PHP package 1.5.0. TinyRustLM.MiRust.com is the developer portal, with the legacy runtime documentation corpus preserved under `/docs/runtime-portal/`. Deep report bodies remain in the linked durable docs rather than duplicated here.

# TinyRustLM

TinyRustLM.MiRust.com is the TinyRustLM developer portal: a plain PHP project website for a zero-dependency Rust/WebAssembly browser-local small language model runtime, custom `.slm` artifacts, deterministic validation, quantized execution, adapter sidecars, selector registries, local-only diagnostics, UAI file memory, durable reports, and project contact routing.

Current public app route:

- <https://TinyRustLM.com/>

Current developer portal route:

- <https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/developer-portal/>

## Core Routes

- [Overview](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/): project summary, constraints, runtime surfaces, and deployment posture.
- [Architecture](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/architecture/): static browser UI, Rust/WASM runtime, offline packer, local server, harness, and claim boundaries.
- [Runtime](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/runtime/): Rust/WASM runtime responsibilities, byte transfer, generation, diagnostics, and error states.
- [.slm Format](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/slm-format/): custom model artifact contract for headers, tensor directory, tokenizer metadata, quantization fields, and checksums.
- [Quantization](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/quantization/): f32, q8_0, q4_0, and the 33,554,432-byte browser selector budget.
- [Browser Runtime](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/browser-runtime/): TinyRustLM Chat mode, local/Hugging Face/P2P source choices, Hugging Face P2P-on-by-default source list, shared simple/advanced source-row actions, safe `.safetensors` source-file hints for local conversion, paired `minimodel.huggingface_conversion_request.v0` plus script downloads, one-command `convert-huggingface-request` local conversion receipt flow, `P2P Import` for MiniModel matches with peer-offer proof plus catalog peer source or Known peer URL, `Set Peer URL` fallback, one-command `prepare-peer-share` sender execution, `add-peer-source` for later consenting peer availability metadata, `write-peer-source-announcement` for portable availability metadata, local peer-source announcement JSON overlay on loaded `models.v0.json`, `apply-peer-source-announcements` for maintainer drift checks, batch `write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcements` publication, metadata-only `write-catalog-snapshot` reuse, local `models.v0.json` loading before Hugging Face search, one-command `import-peer-request` receiver execution, local MiniModel share metadata export after verified `.slm` import, local-only imports, transcript state, and reset boundaries.
- [Adapters](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/adapters/): ADP1, ASP1, and ALR1 adapter sidecars with Rust validation before apply.
- [Model Breeding](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/model-breeding/): offline candidate lineage, parent compatibility, operator receipts, manifests, runtime-smoke, eval evidence, and selector admission.
- [Testing](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/testing/): Rust tests, browser harness checks, WASM ABI smoke, browser smoke modes, and performance soak.
- [Developer Portal](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/developer-portal/): consolidated implementation docs, legacy runtime archive, preserved checksum manifest, proof routes, operations notes, and current app boundary.
- [Roadmap](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/roadmap/): proof-first expansion plan and explicit future boundaries.
- [Glossary](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/glossary/): compact terms for humans and agents.
- [Docs + UAI Memory](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/docs/): durable report archive, long-term memory body, report index, and `.uai` read order.
- [Contact Mike Kappel](https://TinyRustLM.mirust.com/contact/): direct project and architecture contact route.

## Runtime Documentation Consolidation

The former standalone runtime documentation lane is retired as a separate documentation authority. Its public implementation corpus is preserved under `/docs/runtime-portal/` with a checksum-bearing manifest at `/docs/runtime-portal/MANIFEST.md` and a current archive index at `/docs/runtime-portal/index.md`.

Use `/developer-portal/` as the current human-readable route for TinyRustLM developer evidence. Use `https://TinyRustLM.com/` as the current public app route. SLMComposer.com is no longer the canonical public app identity.

## Truth Boundary

TinyRustLM is a browser-local Rust/WebAssembly small language model runtime project. It is not a cloud assistant, hosted chatbot, WordPress theme, generic Rust site, GGUF runtime claim, or remote inference service.

Project servers do not run user model bytes. Project servers do not serve runnable user model bytes. TinyRustLM.com remains browser-local and imports local `.slm` files through the browser file picker.

## Source Options

TinyRustLM should explain model source choices as user-controlled import paths:

- Local: users choose local `.slm` files through the browser file picker.
- Hugging Face: metadata discovery may help users find source candidates, including safe `.safetensors` sibling hints for local conversion, but rows are not runnable unless MiniModel metadata names an admitted `.slm` with peer-offer proof and a catalog-listed or user-supplied consenting peer source. The simple and advanced result rows share action/source-note helpers so `P2P Import`, `Set Peer URL`, `Start Conversion`, disabled-P2P fallback, and source hints stay aligned. The simple list defaults P2P on, shows `P2P Import` only for proof-ready matches with a validated `peer_sources` row or saved Known peer URL, shows `Set Peer URL` for proof-ready matches without a known source, shows `Start Conversion` otherwise, and warns once when P2P is disabled. P2P import writes that consenting direct `http://` peer into the local Rust reverify handoff; the receiver script calls `minimodel import-peer-request <request-json> <manifest> <output-dir>`. Catalog peer sources are metadata, not hosted bytes. Start Conversion saves both a `minimodel.huggingface_conversion_request.v0` JSON file and paired script; the script runs one TinyRustLM packer command, `convert-huggingface-request <request.json> <input.safetensors> <output-dir> [source-shape] [quantization]`, against a user-owned local `.safetensors`, writes `tinyrustlm-conversion.receipt`, then calls `minimodel prepare-peer-share` to write proof-ready MiniModel manifest, `.minimodel-peer-offer` proof, local peer pieces, and catalog entry. If a consenting peer URL is available, `minimodel add-peer-source <catalog-entry-json> <output-json> <known-peer-base-url>` writes a with-peer entry and `minimodel write-peer-source-announcement <catalog-entry-json> <announcement-json> <known-peer-base-url>` writes portable availability metadata; catalog maintainers use `minimodel apply-peer-source-announcements <catalog-entry-json> <output-json> <announcement-json>...` to reject drift before shared catalog publication or `minimodel write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcements <models.v0.json> <catalog-entry-json>... --announcements <announcement-json>...` to batch-publish checked metadata. `minimodel write-catalog-snapshot` then produces metadata-only `models.v0.json` without downloading or hosting model bytes. Users can load that local snapshot before Hugging Face search and can apply a local peer-source announcement JSON overlay when the snapshot is proof-ready but lacks a peer URL, so matching rows become P2P-ready without a default catalog fetch. Project servers still must not run, proxy, or serve user model bytes.
- Share metadata: after a verified local `.slm`, TinyRustLM can save `minimodel.local_slm_share_metadata.v0` with a catalog-entry candidate, artifact SHA256, fixed-size chunk hashes, chunk-list SHA256, Merkle root, and live transfer flags set unavailable.
- Peer-to-peer: future transfer work must start with secure metadata, Rust `.minimodel-peer-offer` proof, checksums, consent, one-command `prepare-peer-share` sender output, late `add-peer-source` metadata publication, portable `write-peer-source-announcement` metadata, maintainer-side `apply-peer-source-announcements` drift checks, batch `write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcements` publication, metadata-only `write-catalog-snapshot` reuse, and Rust verification before any broader peer networking.

All source options must converge on local Rust validation before a model is admitted.

## Rust Responsibilities

Rust owns `.slm` parsing, tokenizer behavior, tensor validation, quantization math, KV cache state, sampling, generation, diagnostics, error codes, adapter validation, adapter application, checksum verification, and local import receipts.

JavaScript owns browser controls, local file selection, byte transfer into WASM memory, transcript rendering, and diagnostics display. JavaScript must not parse tensor payloads or make model-quality claims.

## Artifact Rules

`.slm` is the custom local model artifact. Public copy should keep the following fields visible:

- magic and schema version
- model id and artifact kind
- byte count
- tensor directory
- tokenizer metadata
- quantization fields
- artifact checksum
- tokenizer and config checksums
- bounded runtime state
- optional adapter and selector compatibility metadata

Adapters ADP1, ASP1, and ALR1 are sidecars, not replacement models. They are not applied until Rust validates shape, identity, checksums, tokenizer agreement, tensor layout, and finite payload values.

## Model Exchange Boundary

The future MiniModel/TinyRustLM exchange architecture is metadata-first:

- catalogs may publish schemas, manifests, public keys, model-card routes, license routes, eval routes, and takedown or contact routes
- manifests must be checksum-bound and signature-aware
- Hugging Face source ids can become MiniModel metadata only after review, conversion, Rust validation, runtime smoke, and admission evidence
- verified local `.slm` imports can export share metadata, and converted `.slm` files can use MiniModel `prepare-peer-share`, `add-peer-source`, `write-peer-source-announcement`, `apply-peer-source-announcements`, `write-catalog-snapshot-with-announcements`, and `write-catalog-snapshot` to carry Rust peer-offer proof, local pieces, locally loadable metadata-only catalog reuse, consenting peer-source metadata, and chunk/Merkle fields before broader networking exists
- users must consent before transfer or import
- third-party model entries are not endorsements
- project infrastructure must not host, run, or serve user model bytes

Peer networking remains a later phase. Rust-native QUIC/blob transfer, Rust-libp2p, BitTorrent-style chunking, Iroh, Pear/Bare/Hypercore, and Hugging Face-assisted discovery can be compared later without making a JavaScript runtime a core dependency by default.

## Public Claim Boundaries

- Do not infer cloud inference or remote model execution.
- Do not claim trained assistant quality unless an evaluation sidecar with passed cases exists.
- Do not claim GGUF import support unless a specific conversion path and smoke evidence are added.
- Do not describe this package as WordPress.
- Do not introduce Bootstrap, jQuery, Tailwind, React, Vue, Composer, npm, CDN dependencies, analytics, telemetry, remote inference APIs, or external model downloads by default.
- Treat model and adapter licenses as artifact-specific.

## Agent Behavior

Read visible pages, cite canonical routes, follow robots and terms, respect the no-server-model-bytes boundary, and no-op unsupported requests. When durable memory and a UI page disagree, prefer the newest checksum-bearing durable memory entry and flag the discrepancy for review.
